notes:
The whole list is on n12.jpg (printed page 5), under the heading "East Coast of Scotland." Its footnotes start there and run onto n13.jpg (page 6). n10 and n11 are running text only.

Layout: the asterisk columns are headed '79 '80 '81 '82 '83. No type ("L.H."/"L.V.") and no light characters are printed. The figures are heights: "230 ft." in the first row, then ditto marks (",,"). The sub-headings are Orkney and Mainland, in small caps. Rows 4–7 and Fair Isle come straight under the section heading, so I gave them coast "East Coast of Scotland". The Fair Isle line reads "Land Notes.—7B. Fair Isle.", with B as a small capital. It has no asterisks and no height. Numbers 1–3 are not printed.

Asterisks: I assigned each one to a year by its position under the header. The single stars at nos. 6, 21 and 24 are the least certain, because they're isolated. The '83 column holds 12 stars (nos. 4, 7, 10, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20, 26, 27, 28). The text on n11 says "Twelve stations on this coast have sent in forty-two schedules out of the twenty-six E.C. stations of Scotland". So the stars almost certainly mark the years each station sent returns, though no sentence says so. Nos. 4–29 make 26 stations, which matches "twenty-six" when Fair Isle is left out. Small strokes among the asterisks at nos. 5 and 8, and a dot before no. 27, look like print blemishes.

Keepers: I dropped the full stop that ends each row from the name ("J. Edgar." became "J. Edgar"); it is kept in "printed". "W.Davidson" is printed with no space, and I kept that.

Footnotes:
- † Mr. D. McDonald moved from Pentland Skerries to Skervuile (W. C.) about July 26th and sent returns until then. After that Mr. J. Gilmour took over the returns.
- ‡ The first schedule from Tarbat Ness came from Mr. W. Davidson (Aug. 15–Oct. 30, eleven entries). The note goes on to page 6 with his letter of Jan. 20th, 1884.
- § At Chanonry the schedule was "again" returned by Mr. McGill, who came there in summer 1882.
- || (Kinnaird Head) "Mr. D. M. Scott, who left this station, removed to Sumburgh Head." So Scott was at Kinnaird Head before Sumburgh, and no keeper is printed for Kinnaird Head in 1883.
- ¶ "No Birds" at Montroseness was the reason given for no returns in 1882.
- Page 6 also thanks "Mr. Alexander Greig" for the first return from Noss Head, which gives the full first name of A. Greig.

Copied as printed:
- "Chanonry, Point Elgin": the comma is misplaced (it should read Chanonry Point), and the point is on the Ross side of the Moray Firth, not in Elgin. I recorded name "Chanonry" and place "Point Elgin" exactly as printed.
- "Whalsey" (usually Whalsay), "Girdleness", "Montroseness", "Inch Keith", "North Ronaldshay" and "Cantick Head" are all as printed.
- "D. Laidlaw." is printed for both Dunnet Head (15) and Holborn Head (16). This could be a repeated line or one keeper for both; check against other years.
- J. McDonald (Auskerry) and D. McDonald (Pentland Skerries) are printed as different people.

OCR corrections confirmed from the image: Sumburgh is 300 (OCR "3800"), Pentland Skerries 170 (OCR "270"), Buchan Ness 130 (OCR "180"), Start Point 80 and Cantick Head 115. "J. dack" in the OCR is J. Jack, and "Mife Coast" is Fife Coast.
